text:
anna: CI linkcheck failed for /guides/auth#token-flow — anchor 404 after redirects. noticed after yesterday's nginx redirect PR. @sam any idea?
sam: I pulled that nginx PR yesterday. There were a couple catch-all redirects for renamed slugs. fragments themselves aren't sent to server, but if final page changed header ids it can break linkcheck.
liam: fragments don't travel on HTTP, correct. linkcheck follows redirect and then looks for the id on the resulting page. if the new page no longer has #token-flow it'll fail.
anna: digging into the PR now — it renamed auth.md -> oauth-auth.md and added a generic redirect from /guides/auth -> /guides/oauth-auth. the redirect is fine, but we didn't map the old anchor to the new header id.
docs-bot: linkcheck: https://buildkite.example/1234/artifacts/linkcheck.log -> 1 broken fragment found: /guides/auth#token-flow -> 404 anchor
sam: quick choices: (a) update redirect to include fragment mapping (b) add an HTML anchor to the new page that matches the old id (c) update all known incoming links. (a) is least effort for immediate fix.
anna: agree. I'll open a tiny PR to change the redirect to include the fragment target. example redirect entry:
```
- from: /guides/auth
  to: /guides/oauth-auth#token-flow
  status: 302
```
I'll also add a short note in the docs CHANGELOG so support knows old deep links are preserved. cc @sam
sam: tiny nit — use 302 for now so we can revert if something odd shows up.
liam: long-term we should generate fragment-aware redirect map during the migration, but this patch is fine.
anna: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1789 — includes redirect + changelog note. requesting review from @sam and @liam.
deploy-bot: buildkite: queued linkcheck job #567 for PR 1789 -> https://buildkite.example/567
docs-bot: linkcheck: PR 1789 linkcheck run passed — fragment resolved :white_check_mark: 
anna: closing the loop. will follow up with a migration task to generate map for bulk renames. thanks! :heart:
